newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian zinc output to rise 8.2 pct - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian zinc output to rise 8.2 pct - ABARE.

text.p: Australian zinc mine production is expected to rise 8.2 percent to 1.12 million tonnes in 1996/97 after climbing 13 percent in 1995/96, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.

In its September quarter report released on Tuesday, ABARE said the 1996/97 forecast was based on the assumption that the McArthur River mine, owned 70 percent by MIM Holdings Ltd, would reach full production capacity.
Zinc export earnings were forecast to increase 12 percent to US$912 million in 1996/97 as a result of further rises in export volumes and expected price rises.
World zinc prices were forecast to rise 12.1 percent to US$1,155 per tonne or 52 U.S. cents per pound in the 1997 calendar year.

"World prices are forecast to rise in 1997 as demand in the infrastructure and automobile sectors increases with stronger world economic growth," ABARE, the government's main commodity forecaster, said in the report.

It said stocks were expected to fall to around 5.8 weeks of consumption by the end of calendar 1997 with world zinc consumption forecast to move ahead of production next year as world economic growth strengthened.
World zinc demand was forecast to grow by less than 1.0 percent to 7.43 million tonnes in calendar 1996, following a strong increase in 1995.
However, ABARE forecast that world zinc demand to rise by 3.0 percent to 7.65 million tonnes in 1997.
"This forecast is driven by expectations of stronger growth in industrial production in OECD countries, and by strong economic and industrial production growth in Asia," ABARE said.
